chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the menstruating woman, what is permissible for her husband from her? He said: Whatever is besides the private part.

key_terms.الْفَرْج: The private part (specifically the vulva/vagina in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is permissible for a husband to do with his wife during her menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the fiqh of intimacy during menstruation, distinguishing between the prohibited act of vaginal intercourse and the permissibility of other forms of closeness. This ruling is derived from the Quranic phrase 'go back to them' in Surah Al-Baqarah, which Shia scholars interpret as allowing general sexual relations excluding the specific organ of intercourse. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the nuances of marital intimacy within the state of hayd.
